import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture

An *abstract elementary class* (AEC) is a class $K$ of structures in a first-order language
$L = L(K)$ together with a partial order $\prec_K$ ("strong substructure") on $K$, refining the
substructure relation, closed under isomorphisms, satisfying coherence, the Tarski–Vaught chain
axioms and a Löwenheim–Skolem axiom. The *Löwenheim–Skolem number* $\operatorname{LS}(K)$ is the
least cardinal $\mu \ge |L(K)| + \aleph_0$ such that every subset $A$ of a model $M \in K$ is
contained in some $N \prec_K M$ with $\|N\| \le |A| + \mu$.

$K$ is *categorical* in a cardinal $\kappa$ if it has exactly one model of cardinality $\kappa$
up to isomorphism.

Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture: for every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal
$\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an AEC $K$ with $\operatorname{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ is categorical in a
cardinal $\ge \mu(\lambda)$, then it is categorical in all cardinals $\ge \mu(\lambda)$.

Since Mathlib has no notion of abstract elementary class, this file defines one. Strong
substructures are encoded by a class of `L`-embeddings, the `K`-embeddings: an `L`-embedding
`f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding exactly when `f[M] ≺_K N`. Unions of chains are encoded by
`FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit`. The language, the models and all cardinals live in a single
universe `u`, which plays the role of the set-theoretic universe; the statement is
universe-polymorphic.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Abstract elementary class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_elementary_class)
- [S. Shelah, *Categoricity for abstract classes with amalgamation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9809197)
- [W. Boney, *Tameness from large cardinal axioms*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0550)
-/
namespace ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture
open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Cardinal
universe u
variable (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u})

blocks.code:
structure AbstractClass where
  /-- `IsModel M` means that the `L`-structure `M` belongs to the class `K`. -/
  IsModel : ∀ (M : Type u) [L.Structure M], Prop
  /-- `IsStrong f` means that the `L`-embedding `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding, i.e.
  `f[M] ≺_K N`. -/
  IsStrong : ∀ {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N], (M ↪[L] N) → Prop
blocks.docstring:
The data underlying an abstract elementary class: a class `K` of `L`-structures (with
universes in `Type u`) together with a class of `L`-embeddings between them, the `K`-embeddings.
An `L`-embedding `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding exactly when `f[M] ≺_K N`, where `≺_K` is the
strong substructure relation of `K`. In particular, for a substructure `N ≤ M`, `N ≺_K M` means
that the inclusion `N.subtype` is a `K`-embedding.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.Theory.ModelType / Set (CategoryTheory.Bundled L.Structure) (only classes of models of a first-order theory, no ≺_K relation); FirstOrder.Language.ElementarySubstructure (only first-order elementary substructures).
justification.name: ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture.AbstractClass
justification.why_needed: Data of an AEC: a class of L-structures (`IsModel`) together with a class of L-embeddings, the K-embeddings (`IsStrong f` ⇔ f[M] ≺_K N). Needed because Mathlib has no abstract elementary classes; the strong-substructure relation must be encoded via embeddings since Lean types cannot literally be subsets of one another.

blocks.name: AbstractClass
blocks.text:
/-- The data underlying an abstract elementary class: a class `K` of `L`-structures (with
universes in `Type u`) together with a class of `L`-embeddings between them, the `K`-embeddings.
An `L`-embedding `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding exactly when `f[M] ≺_K N`, where `≺_K` is the
strong substructure relation of `K`. In particular, for a substructure `N ≤ M`, `N ≺_K M` means

structure AbstractClass where
  /-- `IsModel M` means that the `L`-structure `M` belongs to the class `K`. -/
  IsModel : ∀ (M : Type u) [L.Structure M], Prop
  /-- `IsStrong f` means that the `L`-embedding `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding, i.e.
  `f[M] ≺_K N`. -/
  IsStrong : ∀ {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N], (M ↪[L] N) → Prop
variable {L}
namespace AbstractClass

blocks.docstring:
`K.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ` means that `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` and that every subset `A` of a
model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib; Mathlib's downward Löwenheim–Skolem (`FirstOrder.Language.exists_elementarySubstructure_card_eq`) is only for first-order elementary substructures.
justification.name: ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture.AbstractClass.IsLowenheimSkolemBound
justification.why_needed: The Löwenheim–Skolem axiom with bound μ: μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀ and every subset A of a model M ∈ K lies in a substructure N with N ≺_K M and ‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ. Used both as the LS axiom of an AEC and to define LS(K).

blocks.name: IsLowenheimSkolemBound
blocks.text:
/-- `K.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ` means that `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` and that every subset `A` of a
model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
def IsLowenheimSkolemBound (K : AbstractClass L) (μ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ μ ∧ ∀ (M : Type u) [L.Structure M], K.IsModel M → ∀ A : Set M,
    ∃ N : L.Substructure M, A ⊆ N ∧ #N ≤ #A + μ ∧ K.IsStrong N.subtype

blocks.code:
noncomputable def lowenheimSkolemNumber (K : AbstractClass L) : Cardinal.{u} :=
  sInf {μ | K.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ}
blocks.docstring:
The Löwenheim–Skolem number `LS(K)` of `K`: the least cardinal `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` such that
every subset `A` of a model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`.

justification.name: ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture.AbstractClass.lowenheimSkolemNumber
justification.why_needed: LS(K) := sInf of the set of Löwenheim–Skolem bounds (nonempty by the AEC axiom, so the sInf is attained; the set is upward closed, so LS(K) ≤ λ iff λ is a bound).

blocks.name: lowenheimSkolemNumber
blocks.text:
/-- The Löwenheim–Skolem number `LS(K)` of `K`: the least cardinal `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` such that
every subset `A` of a model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
noncomputable def lowenheimSkolemNumber (K : AbstractClass L) : Cardinal.{u} :=
  sInf {μ | K.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ}

blocks.code:
def Categorical (K : AbstractClass L) (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∃ (M : Type u) (_ : L.Structure M), K.IsModel M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ (M N : Type u) [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N],
      K.IsModel M → K.IsModel N → #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)
blocks.docstring:
`K.Categorical κ` means that `K` has exactly one model of cardinality `κ` up to
isomorphism.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has `FirstOrder.Language.Theory` notions (e.g. completeness, `numberOfCountableModels` in VaughtConjecture.lean), but nothing for categoricity of a class of structures in a given cardinal.
justification.name: ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture.AbstractClass.Categorical
justification.why_needed: K is categorical in κ: there is a model of K of cardinality κ, and any two models of K of cardinality κ are L-isomorphic (exactly one model up to isomorphism).

blocks.name: Categorical
blocks.text:
/-- `K.Categorical κ` means that `K` has exactly one model of cardinality `κ` up to
isomorphism. -/
def Categorical (K : AbstractClass L) (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∃ (M : Type u) (_ : L.Structure M), K.IsModel M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ (M N : Type u) [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N],
      K.IsModel M → K.IsModel N → #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)
end AbstractClass

blocks.code:
structure AbstractElementaryClass extends AbstractClass L where
  /-- `≺_K` is a relation on `K`. -/
  isModel_of_isStrong {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] {f : M ↪[L] N} :
    IsStrong f → IsModel M ∧ IsModel N
  /-- Every isomorphism out of a member of `K` is a `K`-embedding. -/
  isStrong_equiv {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] :
    IsModel M → ∀ e : M ≃[L] N, IsStrong e.toEmbedding
  /-- `K`-embeddings are closed under composition. -/
  isStrong_comp {M N P : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure P]
    {f : M ↪[L] N} {g : N ↪[L] P} : IsStrong f → IsStrong g → IsStrong (g.comp f)
  /-- Coherence: if `g` and `g ∘ f` are `K`-embeddings, then so is `f`. -/
  isStrong_of_comp {M N P : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure P]
    {f : M ↪[L] N} {g : N ↪[L] P} : IsStrong g → IsStrong (g.comp f) → IsStrong f
  /-- Chain axiom: the union of a `≺_K`-chain is in `K`. -/
  isModel_directLimit {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → IsModel (Language.DirectLimit G f)
  /-- Chain axiom: every member of a `≺_K`-chain is a strong substructure of the union. -/
  isStrong_directLimit_of {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → ∀ i, IsStrong (Language.DirectLimit.of L ι G f i)
  /-- Chain axiom: if every member of a `≺_K`-chain is a strong substructure of `N`, then so is
  the union. -/
  isStrong_directLimit_lift {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] {N : Type u} [L.Structure N]
    (g : ∀ i, G i ↪[L] N) (Hg : ∀ i j hij x, g j (f i j hij x) = g i x) :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → (∀ i, IsStrong (g i)) →
      IsStrong (Language.DirectLimit.lift L ι G f g Hg)
  /-- Löwenheim–Skolem axiom. -/
  exists_isLowenheimSkolemBound : ∃ μ, toAbstractClass.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ
blocks.docstring:
An *abstract elementary class* (AEC) in the language `L`, with models in `Type u`.

It is given by a class `K` of `L`-structures together with the strong substructure relation
`≺_K`, encoded by the class of `K`-embeddings (`IsStrong`), subject to the following axioms.
* `≺_K` is a relation on `K`: a `K`-embedding goes between members of `K`.
* Isomorphisms: every isomorphism out of a member of `K` is a `K`-embedding (in particular `K` is
  closed under isomorphism and `≺_K` is reflexive on `K`), and `K`-embeddings are closed under
  composition (`≺_K` is transitive and respects isomorphisms).
* Coherence: if `M₁ ⊆ M₂ ≺_K M₃` and `M₁ ≺_K M₃`, then `M₁ ≺_K M₂`.
* Tarski–Vaught chain axioms: if `(Mᵢ)ᵢ` is a `≺_K`-chain indexed by a nonempty well-ordered
  type, then its union `⋃ᵢ Mᵢ` (the direct limit) is in `K`, `Mᵢ ≺_K ⋃ᵢ Mᵢ` for every `i`, and
  `⋃ᵢ Mᵢ ≺_K N` whenever `Mᵢ ≺_K N` for every `i`.
* Löwenheim–Skolem axiom: there is a cardinal `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` such that every subset `A` of a
  model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib (searched ModelTheory/ for AEC, abstract elementary, Löwenheim, categorical) or in FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
justification.name: ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture.AbstractElementaryClass
justification.why_needed: The AEC axioms on an AbstractClass: K-embeddings go between members of K; every isomorphism out of a member of K is a K-embedding; closure under composition; coherence; the Tarski–Vaught chain axioms (union of a ≺_K-chain indexed by a nonempty well-ordered type is in K, each member is ≺_K the union, and the union is ≺_K N whenever each member is), encoded with `FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit`, `DirectLimit.of` and `DirectLimit.lift`; existence of a Löwenheim–Skolem bound.

variable (L) in
/-- An *abstract elementary class* (AEC) in the language `L`, with models in `Type u`.

It is given by a class `K` of `L`-structures together with the strong substructure relation
`≺_K`, encoded by the class of `K`-embeddings (`IsStrong`), subject to the following axioms.
* `≺_K` is a relation on `K`: a `K`-embedding goes between members of `K`.
* Isomorphisms: every isomorphism out of a member of `K` is a `K`-embedding (in particular `K` is
  closed under isomorphism and `≺_K` is reflexive on `K`), and `K`-embeddings are closed under
  composition (`≺_K` is transitive and respects isomorphisms).
* Coherence: if `M₁ ⊆ M₂ ≺_K M₃` and `M₁ ≺_K M₃`, then `M₁ ≺_K M₂`.
* Tarski–Vaught chain axioms: if `(Mᵢ)ᵢ` is a `≺_K`-chain indexed by a nonempty well-ordered
  type, then its union `⋃ᵢ Mᵢ` (the direct limit) is in `K`, `Mᵢ ≺_K ⋃ᵢ Mᵢ` for every `i`, and
  `⋃ᵢ Mᵢ ≺_K N` whenever `Mᵢ ≺_K N` for every `i`.
* Löwenheim–Skolem axiom: there is a cardinal `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` such that every subset `A` of a
  model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
structure AbstractElementaryClass extends AbstractClass L where
  /-- `≺_K` is a relation on `K`. -/
  isModel_of_isStrong {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] {f : M ↪[L] N} :
    IsStrong f → IsModel M ∧ IsModel N
  /-- Every isomorphism out of a member of `K` is a `K`-embedding. -/
  isStrong_equiv {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] :
    IsModel M → ∀ e : M ≃[L] N, IsStrong e.toEmbedding
  /-- `K`-embeddings are closed under composition. -/
  isStrong_comp {M N P : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure P]
    {f : M ↪[L] N} {g : N ↪[L] P} : IsStrong f → IsStrong g → IsStrong (g.comp f)
  /-- Coherence: if `g` and `g ∘ f` are `K`-embeddings, then so is `f`. -/
  isStrong_of_comp {M N P : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure P]
    {f : M ↪[L] N} {g : N ↪[L] P} : IsStrong g → IsStrong (g.comp f) → IsStrong f
  /-- Chain axiom: the union of a `≺_K`-chain is in `K`. -/
  isModel_directLimit {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → IsModel (Language.DirectLimit G f)
  /-- Chain axiom: every member of a `≺_K`-chain is a strong substructure of the union. -/
  isStrong_directLimit_of {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → ∀ i, IsStrong (Language.DirectLimit.of L ι G f i)
  /-- Chain axiom: if every member of a `≺_K`-chain is a strong substructure of `N`, then so is
  the union. -/
  isStrong_directLimit_lift {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] {N : Type u} [L.Structure N]
    (g : ∀ i, G i ↪[L] N) (Hg : ∀ i j hij x, g j (f i j hij x) = g i x) :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → (∀ i, IsStrong (g i)) →
      IsStrong (Language.DirectLimit.lift L ι G f g Hg)
  /-- Löwenheim–Skolem axiom. -/

namespace AbstractElementaryClass

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isModel_of_equiv (hM : K.IsModel M) (e : M ≃[L] N) : K.IsModel N :=
  (K.isModel_of_isStrong (K.isStrong_equiv hM e)).2
blocks.name: isModel_of_equiv
blocks.text:
/-- `K` is closed under isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isModel_of_equiv (hM : K.IsModel M) (e : M ≃[L] N) : K.IsModel N :=
  (K.isModel_of_isStrong (K.isStrong_equiv hM e)).2

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isStrong_refl (hM : K.IsModel M) : K.IsStrong (Embedding.refl L M) :=
  Language.Equiv.refl_toEmbedding (L := L) (M := M) ▸
    K.isStrong_equiv hM (Language.Equiv.refl L M)
blocks.name: isStrong_refl
blocks.text:
/-- `≺_K` is reflexive on `K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isStrong_refl (hM : K.IsModel M) : K.IsStrong (Embedding.refl L M) :=
  Language.Equiv.refl_toEmbedding (L := L) (M := M) ▸
    K.isStrong_equiv hM (Language.Equiv.refl L M)

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 3]
def univ : AbstractElementaryClass L where
  IsModel _ := True
  IsStrong _ := True
  isModel_of_isStrong _ := ⟨trivial, trivial⟩
  isStrong_equiv _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_comp _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_of_comp _ _ := trivial
  isModel_directLimit _ _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_directLimit_of _ _ _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_directLimit_lift _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ := trivial
  exists_isLowenheimSkolemBound := by
    refine ⟨L.card + ℵ₀, le_rfl, fun M _ _ A => ⟨Substructure.closure L A,
      Substructure.subset_closure, ?_, trivial⟩⟩
    have h := Substructure.lift_card_closure_le (L := L) (s := A)
    simp only [lift_id] at h
    have hF : #(Σ i, L.Functions i) ≤ L.card := by
      rw [card, mk_sum, lift_id, lift_id]
      exact le_self_add
    refine h.trans (max_le ?_ ?_)
    · exact le_add_left le_add_self
    · exact add_le_add_right (hF.trans le_self_add) _
blocks.docstring:
The class of all `L`-structures, with all `L`-embeddings as `K`-embeddings, is an abstract
elementary class (with Löwenheim–Skolem number at most `|L| + ℵ₀`).

justification.name: ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture.AbstractElementaryClass.univ
justification.why_needed: `@[category test]`: the class of all L-structures with all L-embeddings is an AEC (LS axiom verified with `Substructure.lift_card_closure_le`); checks the definition is non-trivially satisfiable. Also two `@[category API]` lemmas `isModel_of_equiv` and `isStrong_refl` show the iso-closure and reflexivity of the classical definition are derivable from the chosen axioms.

@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem shelahs_eventual_categoricity_conjecture :
    ∀ lam : Cardinal.{u}, ∃ μ : Cardinal.{u},
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}) (K : AbstractElementaryClass L),
        K.lowenheimSkolemNumber ≤ lam → (∃ κ, μ ≤ κ ∧ K.Categorical κ) →
          ∀ κ, μ ≤ κ → K.Categorical κ := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture.**
For every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an abstract
elementary class $K$ with $\operatorname{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ is categorical in some cardinal
$\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$, then it is categorical in every cardinal $\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$.

Here $\mu(\lambda)$ depends only on $\lambda$, not on $K$, and "categorical in $\kappa$" means
that $K$ has exactly one model of cardinality $\kappa$ up to isomorphism.
blocks.name: shelahs_eventual_categoricity_conjecture
blocks.text:
/-- **Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture.**
For every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an abstract
elementary class $K$ with $\operatorname{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ is categorical in some cardinal
$\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$, then it is categorical in every cardinal $\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$.

Here $\mu(\lambda)$ depends only on $\lambda$, not on $K$, and "categorical in $\kappa$" means
that $K$ has exactly one model of cardinality $\kappa$ up to isomorphism. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem shelahs_eventual_categoricity_conjecture :
    ∀ lam : Cardinal.{u}, ∃ μ : Cardinal.{u},
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}) (K : AbstractElementaryClass L),
        K.lowenheimSkolemNumber ≤ lam → (∃ κ, μ ≤ κ ∧ K.Categorical κ) →
          ∀ κ, μ ≤ κ → K.Categorical κ := by
  sorry
end ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture

claims.decomposer_note: Single Prop with quantifier order ∀λ ∃μ ∀K (μ depends only on λ, not on K); 'categorical in κ' means exactly one model of cardinality κ up to isomorphism; 'above' is read as ≥ μ(λ) following Boney/Shelah (D.(3a)) and the article (both use ≥), which is equivalent up to adjusting μ; LS(K) ≤ λ vs LS(K) = λ (Boney) are equivalent by taking μ monotone; the AEC definition includes the Löwenheim–Skolem axiom with LS(K) ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀, and the article's convention of ignoring models below LS(K) is immaterial above μ(λ). The article's stronger conjectures (threshold = Hanf number of PC classes; μ_{ℵ₀} = ℶ_{ω₁} for L_{ω₁,ω}) are not posed by the statement and are excluded.
claims.reviewer_why: c06 states exactly ∀λ ∃μ ∀L ∀K, LS(K) ≤ λ → (∃κ ≥ μ, K categorical in κ) → ∀κ ≥ μ, K categorical in κ, with ≥ per the decomposition notes (Boney D.(3a)), and 'categorical in κ' = existence of a model of size κ in K plus uniqueness up to L-isomorphism. Its bespoke AEC is the standard K-embedding presentation (Shelah Def. 0.B) and encodes every axiom of Shelah Def. 0.A / Boney Def. 2.1 / Wikipedia: ≺_K a relation on K, iso-closure + reflexivity (isStrong_equiv), transitivity (isStrong_comp), coherence (isStrong_of_comp), all three Tarski–Vaught clauses for nonempty well-ordered chains via Mathlib DirectLimit (union ∈ K, Mᵢ ≺_K ⋃, smoothness via lift), and LS(K) as the least μ ≥ |L|+ℵ₀ with the downward hull property (sInf of a nonempty set of cardinals). It has API lemmas and a sorry-free `univ` test showing the structure is satisfiable, and passes all repo linters. import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture

An *abstract elementary class* (AEC) is a class $K$ of structures in a first-order language
$L = L(K)$ together with a partial order $\prec_K$ ("strong substructure") on $K$, refining the
substructure relation, closed under isomorphisms, satisfying coherence, the Tarski–Vaught chain
axioms and a Löwenheim–Skolem axiom. The *Löwenheim–Skolem number* $\operatorname{LS}(K)$ is the
least cardinal $\mu \ge |L(K)| + \aleph_0$ such that every subset $A$ of a model $M \in K$ is
contained in some $N \prec_K M$ with $\|N\| \le |A| + \mu$.

$K$ is *categorical* in a cardinal $\kappa$ if it has exactly one model of cardinality $\kappa$
up to isomorphism.

Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture: for every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal
$\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an AEC $K$ with $\operatorname{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ is categorical in a
cardinal $\ge \mu(\lambda)$, then it is categorical in all cardinals $\ge \mu(\lambda)$.

Since Mathlib has no notion of abstract elementary class, this file defines one. Strong
substructures are encoded by a class of `L`-embeddings, the `K`-embeddings: an `L`-embedding
`f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding exactly when `f[M] ≺_K N`. Unions of chains are encoded by
`FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit`. The language, the models and all cardinals live in a single
universe `u`, which plays the role of the set-theoretic universe; the statement is
universe-polymorphic.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Abstract elementary class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_elementary_class)
- [S. Shelah, *Categoricity for abstract classes with amalgamation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9809197)
- [W. Boney, *Tameness from large cardinal axioms*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0550)
-/

namespace ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Cardinal

universe u

variable (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u})

/-- The data underlying an abstract elementary class: a class `K` of `L`-structures (with
universes in `Type u`) together with a class of `L`-embeddings between them, the `K`-embeddings.
An `L`-embedding `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding exactly when `f[M] ≺_K N`, where `≺_K` is the
strong substructure relation of `K`. In particular, for a substructure `N ≤ M`, `N ≺_K M` means
that the inclusion `N.subtype` is a `K`-embedding. -/
structure AbstractClass where
  /-- `IsModel M` means that the `L`-structure `M` belongs to the class `K`. -/
  IsModel : ∀ (M : Type u) [L.Structure M], Prop
  /-- `IsStrong f` means that the `L`-embedding `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding, i.e.
  `f[M] ≺_K N`. -/
  IsStrong : ∀ {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N], (M ↪[L] N) → Prop

variable {L}

namespace AbstractClass

/-- `K.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ` means that `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` and that every subset `A` of a
model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
def IsLowenheimSkolemBound (K : AbstractClass L) (μ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ μ ∧ ∀ (M : Type u) [L.Structure M], K.IsModel M → ∀ A : Set M,
    ∃ N : L.Substructure M, A ⊆ N ∧ #N ≤ #A + μ ∧ K.IsStrong N.subtype

/-- The Löwenheim–Skolem number `LS(K)` of `K`: the least cardinal `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` such that
every subset `A` of a model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
noncomputable def lowenheimSkolemNumber (K : AbstractClass L) : Cardinal.{u} :=
  sInf {μ | K.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ}

/-- `K.Categorical κ` means that `K` has exactly one model of cardinality `κ` up to
isomorphism. -/
def Categorical (K : AbstractClass L) (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∃ (M : Type u) (_ : L.Structure M), K.IsModel M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ (M N : Type u) [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N],
      K.IsModel M → K.IsModel N → #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

end AbstractClass

variable (L) in
/-- An *abstract elementary class* (AEC) in the language `L`, with models in `Type u`.

It is given by a class `K` of `L`-structures together with the strong substructure relation
`≺_K`, encoded by the class of `K`-embeddings (`IsStrong`), subject to the following axioms.
* `≺_K` is a relation on `K`: a `K`-embedding goes between members of `K`.
* Isomorphisms: every isomorphism out of a member of `K` is a `K`-embedding (in particular `K` is
  closed under isomorphism and `≺_K` is reflexive on `K`), and `K`-embeddings are closed under
  composition (`≺_K` is transitive and respects isomorphisms).
* Coherence: if `M₁ ⊆ M₂ ≺_K M₃` and `M₁ ≺_K M₃`, then `M₁ ≺_K M₂`.
* Tarski–Vaught chain axioms: if `(Mᵢ)ᵢ` is a `≺_K`-chain indexed by a nonempty well-ordered
  type, then its union `⋃ᵢ Mᵢ` (the direct limit) is in `K`, `Mᵢ ≺_K ⋃ᵢ Mᵢ` for every `i`, and
  `⋃ᵢ Mᵢ ≺_K N` whenever `Mᵢ ≺_K N` for every `i`.
* Löwenheim–Skolem axiom: there is a cardinal `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` such that every subset `A` of a
  model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
structure AbstractElementaryClass extends AbstractClass L where
  /-- `≺_K` is a relation on `K`. -/
  isModel_of_isStrong {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] {f : M ↪[L] N} :
    IsStrong f → IsModel M ∧ IsModel N
  /-- Every isomorphism out of a member of `K` is a `K`-embedding. -/
  isStrong_equiv {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] :
    IsModel M → ∀ e : M ≃[L] N, IsStrong e.toEmbedding
  /-- `K`-embeddings are closed under composition. -/
  isStrong_comp {M N P : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure P]
    {f : M ↪[L] N} {g : N ↪[L] P} : IsStrong f → IsStrong g → IsStrong (g.comp f)
  /-- Coherence: if `g` and `g ∘ f` are `K`-embeddings, then so is `f`. -/
  isStrong_of_comp {M N P : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure P]
    {f : M ↪[L] N} {g : N ↪[L] P} : IsStrong g → IsStrong (g.comp f) → IsStrong f
  /-- Chain axiom: the union of a `≺_K`-chain is in `K`. -/
  isModel_directLimit {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → IsModel (Language.DirectLimit G f)
  /-- Chain axiom: every member of a `≺_K`-chain is a strong substructure of the union. -/
  isStrong_directLimit_of {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → ∀ i, IsStrong (Language.DirectLimit.of L ι G f i)
  /-- Chain axiom: if every member of a `≺_K`-chain is a strong substructure of `N`, then so is
  the union. -/
  isStrong_directLimit_lift {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] {N : Type u} [L.Structure N]
    (g : ∀ i, G i ↪[L] N) (Hg : ∀ i j hij x, g j (f i j hij x) = g i x) :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → (∀ i, IsStrong (g i)) →
      IsStrong (Language.DirectLimit.lift L ι G f g Hg)
  /-- Löwenheim–Skolem axiom. -/
  exists_isLowenheimSkolemBound : ∃ μ, toAbstractClass.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ

namespace AbstractElementaryClass

variable (K : AbstractElementaryClass L) {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N]

/-- `K` is closed under isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isModel_of_equiv (hM : K.IsModel M) (e : M ≃[L] N) : K.IsModel N :=
  (K.isModel_of_isStrong (K.isStrong_equiv hM e)).2

/-- `≺_K` is reflexive on `K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isStrong_refl (hM : K.IsModel M) : K.IsStrong (Embedding.refl L M) :=
  Language.Equiv.refl_toEmbedding (L := L) (M := M) ▸
    K.isStrong_equiv hM (Language.Equiv.refl L M)

variable (L) in
/-- The class of all `L`-structures, with all `L`-embeddings as `K`-embeddings, is an abstract
elementary class (with Löwenheim–Skolem number at most `|L| + ℵ₀`). -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
def univ : AbstractElementaryClass L where
  IsModel _ := True
  IsStrong _ := True
  isModel_of_isStrong _ := ⟨trivial, trivial⟩
  isStrong_equiv _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_comp _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_of_comp _ _ := trivial
  isModel_directLimit _ _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_directLimit_of _ _ _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_directLimit_lift _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ := trivial
  exists_isLowenheimSkolemBound := by
    refine ⟨L.card + ℵ₀, le_rfl, fun M _ _ A => ⟨Substructure.closure L A,
      Substructure.subset_closure, ?_, trivial⟩⟩
    have h := Substructure.lift_card_closure_le (L := L) (s := A)
    simp only [lift_id] at h
    have hF : #(Σ i, L.Functions i) ≤ L.card := by
      rw [card, mk_sum, lift_id, lift_id]
      exact le_self_add
    refine h.trans (max_le ?_ ?_)
    · exact le_add_left le_add_self
    · exact add_le_add_right (hF.trans le_self_add) _

end AbstractElementaryClass

/-- **Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture.**
For every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an abstract
elementary class $K$ with $\operatorname{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ is categorical in some cardinal
$\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$, then it is categorical in every cardinal $\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$.

Here $\mu(\lambda)$ depends only on $\lambda$, not on $K$, and "categorical in $\kappa$" means
that $K$ has exactly one model of cardinality $\kappa$ up to isomorphism. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem shelahs_eventual_categoricity_conjecture :
    ∀ lam : Cardinal.{u}, ∃ μ : Cardinal.{u},
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}) (K : AbstractElementaryClass L),
        K.lowenheimSkolemNumber ≤ lam → (∃ κ, μ ≤ κ ∧ K.Categorical κ) →
          ∀ κ, μ ≤ κ → K.Categorical κ := by
  sorry

end ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture

items: Encoding of ≺_K: instead of a relation on literal substructures (impossible across distinct Lean types), the AEC carries a class of L-embeddings (K-embeddings), with `IsStrong f` meaning f[M] ≺_K N; for a substructure N ≤ M, N ≺_K M is `IsStrong N.subtype`. This is the standard 'K-embedding'/categorical presentation of AECs and is equivalent to the set-theoretic one by the isomorphism axiom.

Isomorphism axiom stated as 'every isomorphism out of a member of K is a K-embedding' plus closure under composition; K's closure under isomorphism and reflexivity of ≺_K are derived (API lemmas `isModel_of_equiv`, `isStrong_refl`). Antisymmetry of ≺_K is automatic in the set-theoretic version and has no content in the embedding version.

Chain axioms use `FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit` for the union of a chain, indexed by an arbitrary nonempty well-ordered type ι : Type u (equivalent to indexing by a nonzero ordinal γ); the chain hypothesis `∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)` includes i = j, which just says each Mᵢ ∈ K. The clause Mᵢ ≺_K ⋃ Mⱼ is included (present in Shelah's AxIII, Boney's and Baldwin's definitions, omitted in the Wikipedia article's list) since the conjecture is about AECs in the standard sense.

Löwenheim–Skolem: LS(K) = sInf {μ | μ ≥ |L| + ℵ₀ ∧ every A ⊆ M ∈ K lies in some N ≺_K M with #N ≤ #A + μ}, following Wikipedia/Boney; the AEC axiom guarantees the set is nonempty, and it is upward closed, so `LS(K) ≤ λ` is equivalent to λ being a bound. Shelah's own variant (LS'(K) + |τ|) is not used.

Universes: all models, index types and the language live in `Type u` (`L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}`), and all cardinals are `Cardinal.{u}`; the theorem is universe-polymorphic. Since |L| ≤ LS(K) ≤ λ, restricting the language to universe u loses no generality.
'Above μ(λ)' read as ≥ μ(λ) in both hypothesis and conclusion, following Boney/Shelah D.(3a) and the article (equivalent up to adjusting μ). 'LS(K) ≤ λ' kept as in the statement (vs Boney's '= λ').
The Wikipedia article's convention of discarding models of size < LS(K) is not imposed; it is immaterial for categoricity above μ(λ).

For finite λ the hypothesis LS(K) ≤ λ is unsatisfiable (LS(K) ≥ ℵ₀), so those instances are vacuous, exactly as in the informal statement. The empty class is an AEC but never categorical; the class of all L-structures is an AEC (`univ` test).

reviewer_notes: Statement ambiguities: 'above μ(λ)' read as ≥ (Boney/Shelah D.(3a) and the Wikipedia article both use ≥; equivalent up to adjusting μ). 'LS(K) ≤ λ' kept as in the list entry (Boney has = λ; equivalent by taking μ monotone). The Wikipedia AEC definition omits the clause Mᵢ ≺_K ⋃Mⱼ that Shelah/Boney include; the final file includes it, since the conjecture concerns AECs in Shelah's sense. Chains are indexed by nonempty well-ordered ι : Type u (empty chain excluded, otherwise the empty structure would be forced into K); continuity is not required, which is equivalent given the other axioms (Shelah Claim 0.D). Everything lives in one universe u (L : Language.{u,u}, models in Type u, cardinals in Cardinal.{u}); since |L| ≤ LS(K) ≤ λ this loses no generality, and the theorem is universe-polymorphic. The article's convention of discarding models below LS(K) is not imposed (immaterial above μ). The stronger Hanf-number conjectures from the article are not formalized, per the decomposition table. All eight candidates compiled; the choice among c06/c07/c08 is stylistic, they are mathematically equivalent.
